commit_message:
[CodeGen] Fix linkExecutablesInto creating incorrect executable references (#25102)

linkExecutablesInto renames every executable lookup reference to a
source executable (hal.executable.lookup … executable(src)) to the
linked executable. But, an executable can have variants for more than
one backend (&each backend links its own variants in a separate linking
step).

Without the fix, lookups for the remaining variants are renamed to a
linked executable that doesn't contain their variant. The function
references naming the fully-qualified-variant stay correct, but the
executable lookup and the function reference then disagree. At runtime,
in the best case, this fails when the module loads ("device does not
support any variant of executable …").

Fix: Don't rename all root executable lookups to the linked executable.
Instead, point each lookup at whichever executable its function lookups
name.

commit_message:
[HAL] Fix host copies on non-coherent memory

Several runtime helpers copy through host mappings without the cache
maintenance that iree_hal_buffer_map_range requires for memory that is
not IREE_HAL_MEMORY_TYPE_HOST_COHERENT:

* iree_hal_buffer_map_read did not invalidate its source, unlike
  iree_hal_buffer_map_write, which flushes its target.
* iree_hal_buffer_map_copy flushed its target but did not invalidate
  its source.
* iree_hal_device_transfer_range did not invalidate a mappable source
  buffer before reading it.
* iree_hal_buffer_view_generate_buffer did not flush after its callback
  wrote through the mapping.

The RapidCopySubmit CTS test wrote through a mapping without flushing,
so it now flushes as the API requires.

Mesa's Vulkan driver for Intel GPUs (ANV) exposes host-visible memory
that is cached but not coherent, and the Vulkan HAL allocator picks it
for device-local, host-visible buffers. On an Arrow Lake iGPU, six
Vulkan CTS tests fail before this change (two intermittently) and pass
after it.

commit_message:
[CodeGen] Fix linkExecutablesInto creating incorrect executable references (#25102)

linkExecutablesInto renames every executable lookup reference to a
source executable (hal.executable.lookup … executable(src)) to the
linked executable. But, an executable can have variants for more than
one backend (&each backend links its own variants in a separate linking
step).

Without the fix, lookups for the remaining variants are renamed to a
linked executable that doesn't contain their variant. The function
references naming the fully-qualified-variant stay correct, but the
executable lookup and the function reference then disagree. At runtime,
in the best case, this fails when the module loads ("device does not
support any variant of executable …").

Fix: Don't rename all root executable lookups to the linked executable.
Instead, point each lookup at whichever executable its function lookups
name.
